statements.t: We also have investments in other (“OTH”) types of properties, such as land parcels, projects under development (“UDP”) and a behavioral health care hospital.
While we anticipate that adding RIDEA transactions will be positive for our business model, our ability to succeed in this new
segment will be determined by numerous factors, including our ability to identify suitable investments and our relationship with operators of our SHOP communities.
Depending upon the availability and cost of external capital, we anticipate making additional investments in seniors housing communities.

We believe our business model has enabled and will continue to enable us to maintain the integrity of our property investments, including in response to financial difficulties that may be experienced by operators and the variability of cash flow from our SHOP segment.
During the three months ended March 31, 2026, Prestige provided notice of its intent to repay its $179.9 million mortgage loan and we expect them to repay the loan during the fourth quarter of 2026.
We intend to negotiate with the current operator to remove the two communities from the existing master lease.

If the master lease is subsequently amended to remove the two communities that are being marketed for sale, we will reassess these communities on a stand-alone basis for impairment and evaluate whether they meet the criteria for classification as held-for-sale at that time.
During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, we funded capital improvement projects of $9.7 million within our SHOP segment.

We believe that adequate provision has been made for the possibility of loans proving uncollectible, but we will continually evaluate the financial condition of the operations of our seniors housing and health care properties.
In addition, we will monitor our borrowers and the underlying collateral for mortgage loans and will make future revisions to the provision, if considered necessary.
During 2025, we entered into interest rate swaps with maturities of three, four, five and seven years, respectively to effectively lock-in the forecasted interest payments on the Term Loans.
